conventions.convention: K-means uses positive n and p, 1 ≤ K ≤ n, squared Euclidean distances, and unrestricted labelings; empty clusters contribute zero.

Initialization resolves nearest-center ties by smallest index. Later assignments retain the current label whenever it is nearest, otherwise choose the smallest nearest index. Empty centers remain unchanged; stopping requires both labels and centers unchanged.
Gaussian mixtures assume AC, strictly positive weights summing to one, and symmetric positive-definite component covariances. Responsibilities divide weighted component densities by their sum.

The low-variance limit fixes finite data, centers, and positive weights as σ decreases to zero. Tied nearest centers receive limiting weights proportional to their mixture weights. The claim concerns neither optimized parameters nor EM iterates.
The unrestricted Gaussian M-step requires the observations to have full affine span. Covariance updates use the newly updated weighted means and divisor N_k.
Gaussian EM returns θ_0 through θ_T for a supplied positive integer T. Likelihood ascent is nonstrict and asserts neither parameter convergence nor global optimality.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. A finite K-component Gaussian mixture has positive weights summing to one, means in R^p, and symmetric positive-definite covariances; its density is the weighted sum of the displayed Gaussian component functions, and responsibilities are weighted component densities divided by their sum.

Assume AC, positive n,p,K, full affine span of the observations, and a current Gaussian mixture with positive weights and SPD covariances. Every N_k is positive, their sum is n, every weighted scatter S_k is positive definite, and the unique global maximizer of Q over the stated mixture domain is ρ_k=N_k/n, m_k=the weighted mean, V_k=S_k.

Assume AC. For p ≥ 1, μ in R^p and symmetric positive-definite Σ, if Z has independent standard-normal coordinates and X=μ+Σ^(1/2)Z, then X has the displayed Gaussian Lebesgue density φ_p. In particular φ_p is nonnegative and its integral is one.

Initialize labels by nearest centers with smallest-index ties. Repeatedly assign to nearest centers with current-label retention on ties, replace nonempty centers by their sample means, retain empty centers, and stop when both labels and centers are unchanged.

For positive n,p, 1 ≤ K ≤ n, finite data and any initial centers, the specified tie-sensitive Lloyd algorithm terminates. Assignment does not increase the objective and strictly decreases it if a label changes. Center updates do not increase it and strictly decrease it if a nonempty center changes. Terminal labels are nearest-center labels and nonempty centers are their sample means.
For p ≥ 1, distinct symmetric positive-definite A_0,A_1 and 0<t<1, log det((1−t)A_0+tA_1)>(1−t)log det A_0+t log det A_1. If A_0=A_1, equality holds.

For fixed positive n,p,K, data, centers, and positive mixture weights summing to one, the displayed soft assignments converge to weights renormalized over nearest-center ties, and Ψ_σ converges to the sum of minimum squared distances, equivalently the minimum over labelings. No convergence of EM iterates is asserted.

seams_checked.note: Checked the requiring page and alg-weighted-spectral-clustering against alg-lloyd-k-means and its termination theorem. Step 5 applies Lloyd to finitely many rows in R^k, with 1 ≤ k ≤ the active row count, smallest-index initialization ties, later label retention, unchanged empty centers, and stopping only when labels and centers stabilize. The supplied initialization is permitted by Lloyd's arbitrary-initial-centers hypothesis. Neither side claims global optimality or exactly k nonempty output clusters; there is no reverse dependency.
